action: Check whether you run Jira Service Management Data Center (before 10.3.27 or before 11.3.13) or Server 5.12.16 to 5.12.42, or any other Atlassian self-hosted product in the advisory. Read Atlassian's November 17 bulletin and JSDSERVER-16936 and apply the fixed releases.
exec: Self-hosted Jira Service Management needs an update; the Canadian advisory reports no exploitation and names no CVE.
plain: Canada's cyber agency told organisations running their own Atlassian Jira Service Management help-desk software to update it because of a flaw in how the software checks what users are allowed to do.
products: Atlassian Jira Service Management Data Center

key_findings: Affected: Jira Service Management Data Center 10.3.27 and prior and 11.3.13 and prior.
Also affected: Jira Service Management Server versions 5.12.16 to 5.12.42.
The linked Atlassian ticket JSDSERVER-16936 describes improper authorisation in Jira Service Management Data Center.
The advisory names no CVE and makes no statement about exploitation.
recommendations: Review the Atlassian ticket and security advisories page linked from the advisory.
Apply the necessary updates as they become available.

summary: Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1166 covers Atlassian's November 17 bulletin for seven products: Bamboo, Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Fisheye/Crucible, Jira and Jira Service Management. For Jira Service Management it lists Data Center versions before 10.3.27 and before 11.3.13, and Server 5.12.16 to 5.12.42, and links an improper-authorisation ticket. The advisory names no CVE and says nothing about exploitation.
title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issues Atlassian Jira Service Management advisory AV26-1166

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Canadian Centre for Cyber Security document.

review.note: Page says versions prior to 10.3.27 and 11.3.13 (not and earlier) and covers seven Atlassian products; summary and action corrected
